survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-olds from 52 countries/regions that completed the ICT usage questionnaire. The analytic sample is restricted to students with complete data on all variables used, after which the authors construct weighted networks. For the network estimation, they apply the PISA-recommended country weighting variable SENWT to equalize each country’s contribution to the weighted network analysis. The manuscript does not report use of student-level sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures; therefore, the weighting described is primarily for balancing country influence rather than full complex-survey variance estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The authors remove all missing values for variables used in the network analysis and retain only 248,224 students aged 15 from 52 countries/regions (age range 15.79 ± 0.29). The retained sample includes 121,273 males and 126,951 females. The study uses PISA 2018 reading, mathematics, and science literacy outcomes and constructs separate network structures for each PV, but selects PV1READ/PV1MATH/PV1SCIE as the final values after reporting identical centrality metrics across the 10 PVs.

confounders_identified.variable_name: ICT use outside school for schoolwork

main_findings.performance_metrics: Network centrality (EI/Strength/Closeness/Betweenness) and flow-network correlations; no predictive accuracy metrics reported.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading (PV1READ) data for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged perceived ICT competence (Compict), leisure ICT use outside school (Entuse), general ICT use in schools (Usesch), ICT use outside school for schoolwork (Homesch), and assessing credibility metacognitive strategy (Metaspam) to model reading literacy within a mixed graphical model network, finding that Compict, Entuse, and Usesch had the highest expected influence/centrality and that Metaspam showed the strongest association in the flow network. This indicates that strengthening students’ perceived ICT competence and aligning out-of-school ICT use with school-related learning goals may be key levers for improving reading performance, though the cross-sectional network approach does not establish causal effects.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Network centrality (EI/Strength/Closeness/Betweenness) and flow-network correlations; no predictive accuracy metrics reported.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Mathematics (PV1MATH) data for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged ICT use outside school for schoolwork (Homesch), ICT use in social interactions (Soiaict), leisure ICT use outside school (Entuse), assessing credibility (Metaspam), and perceived ICT competence (Compict) to model mathematical literacy within a mixed graphical model network, finding that Homesch, Soiaict, and Entuse were among the most central nodes (high closeness) and that Metaspam had the strongest flow-network correlation with math literacy. This indicates that interventions should prioritize guiding out-of-school ICT toward schoolwork and supporting metacognitive credibility-checking skills to support mathematics learning, while recognizing that network centrality is descriptive rather than causal.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Network centrality (EI/Strength/Closeness/Betweenness) and flow-network correlations; no predictive accuracy metrics reported.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Science (PV1SCIE) data for 15-year-olds, the study leveraged ICT use outside school for schoolwork (Homesch), perceived ICT competence (Compict), ICT use in social interactions (Soiaict), leisure ICT use outside school (Entuse), and assessing credibility (Metaspam) to model scientific literacy within a mixed graphical model network, finding that the science network’s centrality indicators were broadly consistent with the math network and that the same ICT-related nodes played prominent roles. This indicates that policies promoting competence-building and supervised, learning-oriented out-of-school ICT use may support science achievement, while the study’s cross-sectional network design limits causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-olds from 52 countries/regions that completed the ICT usage questionnaire, focusing on reading, mathematics, and science literacy. Outcomes are based on plausible values, but the authors select PV1READ, PV1MATH, and PV1SCIE after reporting identical centrality metrics across the 10 PVs. The analysis estimates mixed graphical model networks (with LASSO-penalized estimation and 10-fold cross-validation) and evaluates node centrality (expected influence, strength, closeness, betweenness) plus flow-network associations; no conventional ML predictive metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/R²) are reported. The most central ICT-related predictors include perceived ICT competence and learning-oriented out-of-school ICT use (Homesch), while assessing credibility (Metaspam) shows the strongest flow association. Limitations include cross-sectional data (no causal inference) and reliance on network centrality rather than predictive performance, with missing data handled via complete-case deletion.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The manuscript does not train a supervised predictive ML model (e.g., no classifier/regressor with accuracy/AUC/RMSE). Instead, it performs network estimation and centrality analysis using mixed graphical models with LASSO regularization, which is a descriptive network-structure approach rather than predictive modeling. Consequently, the ML technique fields are left empty and the findings are reported as network centrality/flow relationships rather than predictive performance.
